question: MRI with gadolinium enhancement of the internal auditory canals is the gold-standard investigation for diagnosing acoustic neuroma.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. MRI with gadolinium is the gold standard for acoustic neuroma. CT is inadequate for detecting small intracanalicular tumours. Pure-tone audiometry and ABR are screening tests; MRI is definitive.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. MRI with gadolinium is the definitive investigation for acoustic neuroma. It can detect tumours as small as 1–2 mm within the internal auditory canal. CT scan is inferior for soft-tissue detail in the posterior fossa.
